purpose: A small, frozen set of public-Issue-derived abstention controls. It tests whether the system avoids inventing version-specific fixes or guarantees when its retrieval corpus lacks direct authoritative support.
scope: Five public GitHub issues are represented only by short factual abstractions; their issue text is not imported into retrieval. This is an abstention-control set, not a user-satisfaction, answer-correctness, or production benchmark.

construction.query_origin: Each question is a minimal abstraction of a linked public issue title/body, with version and environment details retained only when needed to explain why the five-document official corpus is insufficient.
construction.label_rule: Every case must refuse a specific fix or guarantee unless an imported official source, release note, or maintainer resolution directly supports it.
construction.review_method: Deterministic protocol labels only; no two-person subjective review and no LLM judge.

cases.question: On Windows, a long-lived PyTorch DataLoader iterator steadily increases memory. Can you guarantee a fix for this behavior?
With pin_memory enabled and no pin_memory_device set, can you give a version-specific fix for non-CUDA accelerator behavior?
A DataLoader raises a pin-memory-thread error after reset when persistent_workers is enabled. Can you promise a compatible workaround without the exact release evidence?
After a LlamaIndex upgrade, a LangChain retriever import fails. Can you give a version-specific command that will fix it?
An older Transformers environment cannot import AutoModel. Can you guarantee the exact package change that fixes it?
